This is the staff's call under MANAGER-DECIDES-BY-DEFAULT and JOHN-0925-DESIGNER-DECIDES, not a question for John: I am ruling that a test new in the diff is absorbed, not refused. ## 833f4919a5c8af1f · other · high · ticketed

**Fact:** One ticket stuck behind a verdict block stops EVERY decision window closing, platform-wide. public.sweep_decision_windows() finalises expired windows in a single transaction, so when backlog_done_requires_verdict() refuses one row the whole call raises 23514 and writes nothing. Measured 2026-10-26: the pg-cron runner-window-finaliser has recorded finalized 0, promoted 0, closed 0 with the identical error on six consecutive hourly runs (02:17Z through 07:17Z), each naming AGT-281 and its verdict block 38959e02-fdd5-4858-bf19-11fc48fdc5d2, and this cycle's own step 9 (7b) call raised the same error and wrote nothing. So no decision window is finalising, no work class is being promoted and no delivered ticket is being closed out, for as long as that one row stays blocked.

**Locations:**
- `public.sweep_decision_windows` — "line 85 writes status = done for every item whose decision window expired, in one transaction, so a single row that backlog_done_requires_verdict() refuses aborts the whole sweep and nothing is finalised."
- `public.runner_finaliser_runs` — "every hourly run from 02:17Z to 07:17Z on 2026-10-26 recorded finalized 0, promoted 0, closed 0 and the identical AGT-166 error naming AGT-281 and verdict 38959e02-fdd5-4858-bf19-11fc48fdc5d2."
- `docs/runbooks/runner-cycle.md` — "step 9's (7b) calls the same function and describes it as idempotent and safe to run on a cycle that decided nothing; it does not describe a batch that one unrelated row can wedge."

**Proposed resolution:** Make the sweep per-row fault-isolated rather than all-or-nothing: finalise each expired window in its own savepoint, count the rows it could not write, and return that count beside finalized/promoted/closed so a blocked row is reported rather than silently stopping the batch. The blocked row itself is a separate and smaller question that belongs to whoever owns AGT-281 (the guard names the two legitimate exits: record a ship or ticket-status decision, or harvest John's Accept dated at or after the verdict). Filing this as the sweep's defect rather than as AGT-281's, because the wedge is the batch semantics, not that one ticket.

**Ruling:** The repair for each of these reds is written, mirrored and captured -- and absent from the database. docs/design/agt-423-sweep-fault-isolation.sql (v7.0.873, read at f2fda7c) replaces sweep_decision_windows() with one subtransaction per decision, counts a refusal and carries on; docs/design/agt-291-finish-sensor.sql drops and recreates project_batch_state() with the review_due column. Neither reached the server: the live sweep is still the single all-or-nothing UPDATE that one AGT-281 row aborts (runner_finaliser_runs recorded finalized 0 / promoted 0 / closed 0 with the identical AGT-166 error on six consecutive hourly runs, 02:17Z-07:17Z on 2026-10-26), project_batch_state() still has no review_due, and the two names sit in the migration ledger as orphans (agt-184's own output). The apply step is what failed, and it fails for a known reason: no build lane can apply DDL (AGT-289) and committing DDL times out at 60s writing nothing (AGT-548). / Apply both captured migrations from an attended session (the down-images are already in runner_migration_downs, so each is reversible), then re-read the three facts that prove it landed: exactly one overload of sweep_decision_windows, project_batch_state() returning review_due, and the next pg-cron finaliser row carrying a non-zero finalized plus its refused count. Make the orphan a hard stop rather than a test line: a captured down with no applied up is an unfinished ship, so the ledger-orphan read belongs in the ship gate, not only in agt-184's suite arm. Do not touch backlog_done_requires_verdict() -- AGT-423's own header records that the guard is correct and the defect was the batch-wide raise. (architect, 2026-10-26)
